akira.name: Akira
akira.brief: Ransomware group active since March 2023, linked by researchers to former Conti members. Often gets in through VPN and edge-device weaknesses.

aoqin.name: Aoqin
aoqin.brief: Leak site first tracked in November 2026. Posts company size and revenue with payment deadlines. Little public reporting so far.

boobaproject.name: Booba Project
boobaproject.brief: Smaller leak site tracked since July 2026, also posting as "Booba Team". Lists a sector and stolen-data size only. Little public reporting.

braincipher.name: Brain Cipher
braincipher.brief: Ransomware group active since mid-2024, built on leaked LockBit code. Demands ransoms in Monero; often posts bare listings without details.

climax.name: CLIMAX
climax.brief: Leak site first seen in November 2026. Posts only a sector and a website, without samples. Little public reporting so far.

emperador.name: Emperador
emperador.brief: Ransomware-as-a-service first seen in August 2026, at first aimed at Asia-Pacific municipal and government targets. Offers affiliates up to 90%.

everest.name: Everest
everest.brief: Russian-speaking extortion group active since 2020. Also sells network access to other criminals; often uses stolen logins and remote desktop.

incransom.name: INC Ransom
incransom.brief: Prolific ransomware-as-a-service since mid-2023, focused on healthcare, government and education in North America and Europe.

krybit.name: Krybit
krybit.brief: Ransomware-as-a-service launched in March 2026, with lockers for Windows, Linux, ESXi and NAS. Known for a public feud with a rival group.

lockbit5.name: LockBit5
lockbit5.brief: LockBit 5.0: the September 2025 relaunch of the long-running LockBit operation after its 2024 takedown. Targets Windows, Linux and ESXi.

medusalocker.name: MedusaLocker
medusalocker.brief: Ransomware operation active since 2019, not the same as Medusa. Usually gets in through exposed remote desktop and phishing.

n0n.name: N0n
n0n.brief: Data-extortion group tracked since September 2026. Posts anonymised "Company #NN" teasers before naming victims, often with data inventories.

nightspire.name: Nightspire
nightspire.brief: Double-extortion group active since March 2025 that quickly claimed hundreds of victims. Known for ransom deadlines as short as two days.

panzer.name: Panzer
panzer.brief: Ransomware-as-a-service tracked since August 2026; early claims focused on Indonesia. Little public reporting so far.

pixelleaks.name: PixelLeaks
pixelleaks.brief: Leak site first seen in November 2026, posting batches of "verified records" notices with short deadlines. Treat its claims with caution.

play.name: Play
play.brief: Closed ransomware group (also PlayCrypt) active since 2022. Known for exploiting Fortinet and Exchange flaws and for partial encryption.

qilin.name: Qilin
qilin.brief: Ransomware-as-a-service (also Agenda) active since 2022, written in Go and Rust. One of the most prolific leak sites of 2025–26.

rhysida.name: Rhysida
rhysida.brief: Ransomware-as-a-service active since mid-2023. Gets in through phishing and remote access, and auctions stolen data in "lots".

safepay.name: SafePay
safepay.brief: Ransomware group active since late 2024 that runs attacks in-house, without affiliates. Often enters via Cisco firewalls and stolen VPN logins.

soul.name: Soul
soul.brief: Site first seen in November 2026, posting company profiles without proof of stolen data. Its claims are unverified.

thegentlemen.name: The Gentlemen
thegentlemen.brief: Ransomware-as-a-service since mid-2025 (also Storm-2697), with lockers for Windows, Linux and NAS and a 90% share for affiliates.

vortex.name: Vortex
vortex.brief: Data-extortion site first seen in November 2026, claiming Microsoft 365 and Salesforce data. Some of its claims have been called fabricated.

wallstreet.name: Wallstreet
wallstreet.brief: Smaller leak site tracked since June 2026, with no independent public profile yet. Recent claims centred on European engineering firms.
